# f5xc_registration_approval (Resource)

Registration approval action resource

To get more information about f5xc_registration_approval, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/registration#operation/ves.io.schema.registration.CustomAPI.RegistrationApprove)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Registration Approval

# The matching registration must already exist in the PENDING state in the
# system namespace. Approval changes its state to APPROVED.
resource "f5xc_registration_approval" "example" {
  namespace    = "system"
  cluster_name = "example-cluster"
  hostname     = "example-host"
  cluster_size = 1

  retry       = 5
  wait_time   = 30
  tunnel_type = ["SITE_TO_SITE_TUNNEL_IPSEC_OR_SSL"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_name` (String) Cluster name used to locate the registration.
- `cluster_size` (Number) Cluster size override applied to the registration passport.
- `hostname` (String) Hostname used to locate the registration.

### Optional

- `connected_region` (String) Connected region override applied during approval.
- `latitude` (Number) Latitude override applied during approval.
- `longitude` (Number) Longitude override applied during approval.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace used for registration approval operations.
- `private_network_name` (String) Private network name override applied during approval.
- `retry` (Number) Number of polling attempts while locating registrations.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `tunnel_type` (List of String) Tunnel type used during registration approval.
- `wait_time` (Number) Delay in seconds between polling attempts.

### Read-Only

- `registration_name` (String) Resolved registration name approved by this resource.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

#### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell

```
